decisions.advocate: Keep `data-api.binance.vision` as the spot default, but do not close the concern as-is: the build must add an allow-listed host override and must not let the 418 guard depend on a header the mirror may not send.
decisions.decision: Keep data-api.binance.vision as the fixed spot REST host (no switch) and refused fills (451, any non-418 4xx) as gaps with the status; the weight pause must treat a missing X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT-1M as unknown and pause conservatively, pinned by an offline no-header test.
decisions.head: dfe5caa713344b9a03ded3ba6bbe44867b7606d5
decisions.item: Spot REST host and refused fills: the design picks `data-api.binance.vision` as the spot
rationale: Both verdicts agree on the mirror as default and on refusals-as-gaps; the intent names both hosts and proposes 'gaps with the reason', and 418 still stops the run.
The host override is not taken: the intent asks for no option, coding-standards rule 3 forbids unasked scope, and a later small change can add it if the owner wants it.
They disagree on the 418 guard; the safer reading wins: the intent's hard rule is never get the IP banned, and a pause keyed to a header the mirror may not send would be dead code.
A conservative no-header path plus a pinned test closes that gap without widening scope or touching any guardrail.
decisions.reviewer: Accept the design as written (close the concern): `data-api.binance.vision` as the fixed spot default and 451/other-4xx refusals reported as gaps with the status.

decisions.advocate: Do not accept the deferral as written: close the concern at design with a reasoned decision on layout and codec level, and turn the build-time "measurement" into either reproducible evidence or an owner-run check after merge.
decisions.decision: Keep one zstd level-3 Parquet file per day as the intent requires (line 59); the build commits the generator that produces evidence/storage-measurement.md (per-day vs one yearly file, plus a higher zstd level) so the figure is reproducible and labelled synthetic, and the spec gives the owner the real-data check (download BTCUSDT 1m for one year, then cache-info) with a reopen threshold of more than 20% over a single yearly file.
decisions.head: eebc319ba89e2c17afcfc5bd027b36a10bfc1a68
decisions.item: Storage layout and codec level not measured: the intent asked the design to measure one
rationale: Both verdicts agree to keep per-day files; intent line 59 fixes one file per day written atomically, so a month or year layout would contradict a stated requirement.
Neither design nor build can fetch real BTCUSDT data (no allowed domains), so the intent's measurement (line 161) can only be synthetic in-run or real on the owner's machine.

They disagree on whether an uncommitted synthetic figure counts as evidence; the safer reading is the advocate's: commit the generator so a verifier can re-run it, and state that the data is synthetic.
The owner's real-data check with an explicit threshold gives the per-day choice a defined way to be reopened; zstd 3 stays as the default because the codec choice changes no schema or behaviour.
No limit, guardrail or risk-list item is touched; this only shapes the evidence for this item.
decisions.reviewer: Accept the deferral and close the concern as decided: keep one zstd-3 file per day; the build records the measurement as planned (plan step 10) and the owner judges the figure. Not an Important finding.
